value: The variability of NAcc-CEN connectivity weights was significantly higher in cannabis users than controls regardless of task conditions.

model_representation_notes.value: The analysis models task-modulated dynamic connectivity variability, represented as the standard deviation of DCC-derived connectivity weights; the repeated-measures ANOVA included age and average framewise displacement as nuisance covariates.

name.value: NAcc-CEN connectivity variability and during-scan craving

definition.value: The d of NAcc-CEN connectivity for all conditions was significantly correlated with during-scan craving in the positive direction.

value: The variability of dynamic FC between NAcc and the CEN was positively correlated with during-scan craving.
The fluctuations of DA signals in NAcc are constantly affecting some of the major large-scale intrinsic networks.

model_representation_notes.value: The analysis used nonparametric partial Spearman correlation of task-modulated DCC variability with during-scan craving in cannabis users, controlling for age and average framewise displacement, with FDR correction.

name.value: WithinCEN connectivity variability and prescan craving

definition.value: The d of WithinCEN connectivity for all conditions showed a positive correlation with the prescan craving.

spans.text: The   d   of WithinCEN connectivity for all conditions showed a positive correlation with the prescan craving.

value: The variability of dynamic FC within the CEN was positively correlated with prescan craving.
This correlation may imply the involvement of the dysfunctional CEN in managing the craving, reflecting the higher demand of cognitive control over the transient fluctuations of DA signals.

model_representation_notes.value: The analysis used nonparametric partial Spearman correlation of task-modulated DCC variability with prescan craving in cannabis users, controlling for age and average framewise displacement, with FDR correction.

definition.value: The d of modularity was positively correlated with prescan craving.

value: The variability of network modularity was positively correlated with prescan craving.
As the variability of network modularity increases, so does prescan craving.
The unstable segregation of the brain network relates to the loss of DA signal balance, which is potentially more disrupted in cannabis users than the controls.

model_representation_notes.value: The analysis used nonparametric partial Spearman correlation of task-modulated variability in whole-brain modularity with prescan craving in cannabis users, controlling for age and average framewise displacement, with FDR correction.
